newsitem.title: ITALY: Alitalia expands board, unions protest.
newsitem.headline: Alitalia expands board, unions protest.

text.p: State-owned airline Alitalia agreed on Thursday to expand the size of its board to 17 members from 13, drawing criticism from trades unions which said their own weight on the board would be diminished.
The plan was proposed by majority shareholder IRI, Italy's state industrial holding company, and approved by an Alitalia shareholders' meeting.
Alitalia chairman Fausto Cereti said the expansion of the board "shows that the Italian system is pluralistic".
Three trades unions representatives were appointed to the board in May as part of a deal between management and the unions on a restructuring plan designed to end the airline's losses.
They said the enlargement would diminish their ability to represent staff and branded the appointments political.
"I don't understand what right anyone has to allow political party representatives to join the board," one of the union board members, Giuseppe Surrenti, told reporters.
The new members are Maurizio Maresca, Giuseppe Consolo, Virgilio Maxia and Serafino Gatti.
